item.figure_description: A geometric diagram showing a straight horizontal line with points A, O, and B labeled from left to right, where O is between A and B. Three rays emanate upwards from point O into the upper half-plane: ray ON (pointing up and to the left), ray OC (pointing almost straight up, slightly to the right), and ray OM (pointing up and to the right). The angle between ray OM and ray OB is indicated with an arc labeled 40°. The angle between ray ON and ray OC is indicated with an arc labeled x°.

reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.

[Image: A large triangle. The left angle is 45 degrees and the top angle is 65 degrees. A line is drawn on the side between the 45 and 64 degree angle to form two smaller triangles—one adjacent to the larger triangle, and one contained within the larger triangle. reference_items.figure_description: A geometric figure featuring intersecting lines and triangles. A triangle has a horizontal base, a left side with an interior angle of 45° at the bottom-left vertex, and an interior angle of 65° at the top vertex. A line segment extends from the top vertex down to the base. A second line segment extends from a point on the left side of the triangle down and to the right, crossing the first line segment and ending at the rightmost endpoint of the extended horizontal base, where the interior angle is labeled 30°. Near the top vertex, a smaller triangle is bounded by the upper part of the left side, the upper part of the segment from the top vertex, and the crossing segment; the interior angle at the intersection of the two segments is marked with an arc and labeled x.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
